crisis.label: Severe
crisis.detail: Aug 3: Trump canceled planned US strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure (Truth Social, night of Aug 1) at the request of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the UAE, Qatar and Iran, and said a deal covering the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's denuclearization is imminent, with fresh talks beginning today (Newsweek, ABC News, Aug 2). Iran's FM Araghchi says Oman-mediated Hormuz talks have reached their final stages (Xinhua, Aug 2-3). Markets priced out risk premium sharply: Brent -4.9% to $83.61 (Investing.com, Aug 3); TTF -5.1% to 56.06 EUR/MWh (Trading Economics, Aug 3). The strait remains physically closed with no confirmed reopening yet, and the Jul 26-30 pause broke after 5 days, so this de-escalation should be treated as fragile. Tail cut to 45%.

commodityScenario: Aug 3: President Trump canceled planned US strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure over the weekend at the request of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the UAE, Qatar and Iran, and said a deal covering the 'complete and total opening' of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's denuclearization is imminent, with fresh talks set to begin today (Newsweek, ABC News, Aug 2). Iran's FM Araghchi said Oman-mediated negotiations on reopening Hormuz have reached their final stages, though Iran still insists on retaining control and collecting transit fees (Xinhua, Aug 2-3). Markets priced out risk premium sharply: Brent fell 4.9% to $83.61/bbl (Investing.com, Aug 3); TTF fell 5.1% to 56.06 EUR/MWh (Trading Economics, Aug 3); JKM's CFD reference held near $21.45/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Jul 31). The strait remains physically closed, with the last reviewed transit count still 6 vessels/day (Windward, Jul 27). Tail falls to 45%.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Trump's Aug 1-2 strike stand-down and the Oman-mediated 'final stage' Hormuz talks convert into a phased reopening arrangement. Risk premia continue easing and Brent settles toward $75-85/bbl. Probability remains capped because the strait is still physically closed and no ceasefire or reopening has been confirmed yet.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks continue but stall on Iran's insistence on retaining control and collecting transit fees; sporadic incidents persist even as large-scale strikes stay paused. Hormuz remains constrained at wartime-low traffic, keeping Brent in an $85-105/bbl range and TTF elevated. This mirrors the Jul 26-30 pause, which ultimately broke.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The stand-down proves as fragile as the Jul 26-30 pause: talks collapse, US strikes resume against IRGC and strategic targets, and Iran renews drone and missile attacks across US-allied Gulf states and commercial shipping. Brent spikes back toward $105-135+/bbl and JKM exceeds $30/MMBtu.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $90.12 (Aug 1, Yahoo Finance BZ=F) as tanker incidents and Kuwait attacks kept risk elevated -> $83.61 (Aug 3, -4.9%, Investing.com) as Trump canceled planned strikes and called a Hormuz/denuclearization deal 'imminent'. Yahoo's BZ=F feed remained stuck at its Jul 31 print, so Investing.com is used as the confirmed source pending a fresher Yahoo print. Working range narrows to $75-90 base; $85-105 stress; $105-135+ tail.
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.93/MMBtu (Jul 16, Trading Economics) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters Sept-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.45/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Jul 31, +0.35%). Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September (Reuters, Jul 23).
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, +2.71% vs Jul 23, MacroMicro) -> 59.07/MWh (Jul 31, +1.4%, Yahoo Finance TTF=F) as tanker incidents kept the supply-risk premium elevated -> 56.06 EUR/MWh (Aug 3, -5.1%, Trading Economics) as Trump's strike stand-down and the Oman-Iran Hormuz talks eased the risk premium. The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline on persistent Qatar LNG disruption.
priceNarratives.Credit: iTraxx Asia IG est. ~138bp (Aug 3, -7bp); ASEAN HY est. ~478bp (-14bp) as Trump's strike stand-down and progress in the Oman-Iran Hormuz talks eased Gulf risk premia.
